newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania votes, comeback of Landsbergis likely.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania votes, comeback of Landsbergis likely.

text.p: Lithuanians voted on Sunday in the second round of a parliamentary election that is expected to seal the political comeback of independence hero Vytautas Landsbergis in the former Soviet republic.
Polling stations in the Baltic state opened at seven a.m. (0500 GMT) and were to close at 9.p.m. (1900 GMT).
The final result may not be known for several days.

But it was expected to confirm the return to power of Landsbergis, the 65-year-old stocky, bearded former music professor who gained worldwide admiration in 1990-91 when he led Lithuania's bid to free itself from the Soviet Union.
The second round of the election works on a majority vote system with the 65 seats up for grabs to be won by candidates with the highest number of votes. A total of 130 candidates are standing.
The first round of the election held last month allocated blocks in the house to political parties.
Twenty-four parties ran but only five got past the five percent threshhold required to gain entry into parliament, splitting 70 seats of the 141-member parliament.

Landsbergis's Homeland Union party won the most votes in that round, unseating the former communists of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP) in a sweet revenge for his 1992 defeat at the polls.
The Homeland Union Party took 33 of the 70 seats while its future coalition parner, the Christian Democrats, won 11 seats. The LDLP took 10, the Centre Union nine and the Social Democrats seven.

The Homeland Union also grabbed two seats under the majority vote single-mandate system being held today, in which a candidate needs over 50 percent of the votes. Landsbergis and Gediminas Vagnorius, tipped to be prime minister, won over 50 percent of vote so do not need to stand again in Sunday's vote.
The results from four districts were declared invalid and will be held again next spring because less than 40 percent of the eligible voters cast ballots.
